tasks.name: Remove atm run; atm claim hold keeps a claim alive instead
tasks.description:
atm must not be able to run commands (the user's security decision, 2026-11-06): `atm run <id> -- <command>` (`loop run` in the new tree) goes. Today a permission prompt covers the whole line, but once `atm run *` is allowed, any command runs through it unchecked. What it gave, a claim kept alive during a long command (a test suite, a wait on CI), comes from a new `atm claim hold <id>` that runs nothing.

## `claim hold <id>`
- The agent writes `atm claim hold T-1 && npm test` in one Bash call. `claim hold` renews the claim once, starts a detached watcher and returns at once; the shell then runs the command itself. atm never sees it.
- The watcher follows the shell that called `claim hold` (its parent process): it renews the claim at the usual interval (three times per lease) while that process lives, and exits when it is gone. It checks the process's start time as well as its ID, so a reused ID doesn't keep it going.
- It stops after a cap (default 4 hours, `--max` to change it within bounds), and when the claim is released, finished or taken over. It renews only that claim, as that agent, and never fails loudly: an error ends the watcher, and the claim then lapses as usual.
- `--json` prints the claim and the watcher's PID and cap.

## Remove
`loop run` and its code (the child process, the renewal loop, exit-code passing), its tests, and its mentions in the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `push`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md` and the docs (`docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`, `docs/v4/atm-cli.md`, `docs/security-architecture.md`).

## Security
`docs/security-architecture.md`: atm runs no command an agent or a task text passes it, as an invariant with its check (a test that the command tree has no command taking a command to run). The watcher runs nothing and only writes claims; record it as such. Skills change, so the written skill review (§3.3).

## Tests
Scenarios or `claims.test.mjs`: `claim hold` renews while its parent lives and stops when it exits; it stops at the cap; it stops when the claim is released; a reused PID with another start time doesn't count. The changelog and What's new entries go with T-425's release.

notes.text: atm loop run removed; atm claim hold <id> (watcher follows the calling shell by pid+start time, --max 240 min). I24 + static check. Review: the watcher (cli/claims.py), skill wording.

tasks.name: Review decisions as their own commands; guarded exits from review; one skip
tasks.description:
Agreed with the user (2026-11-06). A review decision changes no state; the exits from review need the right decision. T-425 already moved approve and request-changes out of `task state` into `atm task review approve|request-changes <id>`; this finishes the model.

## Review decisions: `atm task review <decision> <id>`
The decision comes before the ID, so a permission prefix tells them apart.
- `approve <id> [--note]`, `review_state: approved`
- `request-changes <id> --reason`, `review_state: changes_requested`
- `reject <id> --reason`, `review_state: rejected` (new)

All three only on a task in review, and the task stays in review. **No skill pre-approves any of them:** they are the user's, and an agent asking for one gets a permission prompt the user answers.

## The exits from review, guarded in atm (`atm-cli/atm/lib/state.py`)
| Decision | Exit (`task state <id> …`) |
|---|---|
| `approved` | `done` |
| `changes_requested` | `in_progress` (its agent first, as now) |
| `rejected` | `todo` (back to the pool, the work dropped) or `skipped` |

Without the matching decision, atm refuses the exit, for an agent and a person alike: nobody passes, reworks or drops a review without the decision. The old `reject` transition (review to todo in one step) goes; `task state <id> todo` from review is the rejected exit.

## One skip
`skipped` from any open state (todo, blocked, in progress, in review; from review only once rejected), with `--resolution wont_do|obsolete|duplicate` and `--duplicate-of`; it releases the claim. `done` loses `--resolution`: done means the work is done.

## Update
- the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `close-sprint`: an approval or a rejection is something the user runs, e.g. `! atm task review approve T-1`; no skill pre-approves `task review`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/task-states.md` (the diagram), `docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: I23 rests on atm's guards (the exits need the decision) and on no skill pre-approving `task review`; its check becomes the scenarios plus `skills.test.ts`
- the dashboard where it shows `review_state` (a `rejected` label)
- the skill review (§3.3), and the changelog with T-425's release

## Tests
Scenarios: each decision, refused outside review; each exit refused without its decision and allowed with it (an agent and a person); skip from each open state, from review only when rejected; done without `--resolution`. `skills.test.ts`: no skill pre-approves `task review`.

notes.text: task review approve|request-changes|reject; exits guarded in atm for everyone (done=approved, todo/skip=rejected, start=rework); skip from any open state; done has no --resolution. Review: state.py guards, cross-worktree record.

tasks.name: Rust: the write path: the lock folder, the change transaction, the claims store
tasks.description:
Slice 3a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 3, split in four: this, then the task states, `task review` and `loop next`): the store's write path, which every later slice writes through.

## Change
- `atm-db`: the task folder's **lock** as the Python atm has it (`db/jsongit/lock.py`): a lock folder with `owner.json`, waited for up to `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, broken when its owner is dead or it is over a minute old, released on exit and on SIGTERM; the same folder, so the Python and the Rust atm can run against one project during the switch (`lock.test.mjs`, and `atm _lock-test`). `porting-to-rust.md` §3 says `std::fs::File::lock`: correct it to the lock folder.
- `atm-db`: the **claims store** (`db/jsongit/claims.py`): where it is (shared by a clone's worktrees), reading it, writing it atomically.
- `atm-db`: the **change transaction** (`JsonGitStore.change`, `db/working.py`): under the lock, read `tasks.json` and the claims store, let the change run, write only what changed (`tasks.json` only when its text changed, with the archive first when tasks move into it), atomically, as `to_json` + newline.
- `atm-lib`: the change's actor and time (`ATM_NOW`, `ATM_AGENT` / the session) as later slices need them.

## Tests
Unit tests for the lock (two holders, a dead owner, an old lock, the timeout) and for writing only what changed; `lock.test.mjs` leaves `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

notes.text: The write path in Rust: the lock folder (Python’s protocol, SIGTERM-safe via `signal-hook`, owner checks via `sysinfo`), the claims store and its snapshot, the change transaction (`Store::change`, `Working`), `atm _lock-test`; `lock.test.mjs` passes (6 off the list); porting doc §3 corrected

tasks.name: Windows: the stress test (16 agents in two worktrees) fails
tasks.description:

## What CI showed
- With atm's 10 s lock wait: agents time out waiting for the lock (`timed out waiting for the lock …/wt2/.agentic-task-manager/.lock`).
- With the test's lock wait raised to 60 s on Windows (decided with Hakan, `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`): the test fails after 29 s, with the cleanup's `EPERM` on the test's folder, which hides the assertion underneath: some process still has the folder open.

- What still holds the folder: an atm process that outlives the test (a `claim hold` watcher not ending with its shell on Windows is a suspect: the same `EPERM` shows in `claims.test.mjs`'s watcher test), or a slow exit.
- Whether the lock is slow on Windows (git and process starts there are several times slower), and whether agents queue longer than they should.

The test passes on CI's Windows runner, ideally at atm's default lock wait.

tasks.description:
The first release without the plugin: `dev/0.33.0` to `main`, tagged, built, signed and published, with the formula and the first export of the skills to `solo-swe/skills`. The release process is in [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md).

## On `dev/0.33.0`
- **Version:** `0.33.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.

- **Security checklist** (`docs/security-architecture.md` §3): the skills and `docs/agent/` changed, so do a written review of the skills in §3.3 instead of the live sandbox run. Check that the T-454 entry describes what shipped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm run verify` in `dashboard/`; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo deny check` from the root.

## The PR

- Check the draft (six assets: five archives and `SHA256SUMS`), then publish it.

tasks.name: A release whose tasks merge in several PRs is never released
tasks.description:
`atm vcs pushed --pr <n>` releases a planned release only when **all** its tasks are merged **in that PR** (`release_with_merge` in [code.rs](crates/atm-lib/src/code.rs)). Release 0.32.0's sprint, *The Rust port*, merged in two PRs: #39 (32 tasks), then #40 (the other 5, which shipped in 0.33.0). Recording #39 said `0.32.0 stays planned: T-453, … are not merged in PR #39`, and recording #40 said the same about #39's 32 tasks. So 0.32.0 stays planned although every one of its tasks is merged.

## Change
- A release is released when every one of its tasks is merged (`merged_at` set), whichever PR merged it. Its release time is the last merge. The message names the tasks that keep it planned because they aren't merged yet, not because they merged in another PR.
- `atm vcs pushed` releases such a release the next time it runs. `atm doctor` (or `atm release list`) points out a planned release whose tasks are all merged, so this repo's 0.32.0 can be fixed by running it again.

## Tests
A scenario in `tests/scripts/scenarios/`: a release whose tasks are in two PRs stays planned after the first merge and is released by the second; a release with one PR still works as it does now.

notes.text: A release is released once all its tasks are merged, in any PR (released_at its last merge); messages say "not merged yet"; atm doctor warns about a planned release whose tasks are all merged. Scenarios in pr.json and releases.json. This repo’s 0.32.0 is released by `atm vcs pushed --pr 40` once this atm is installed.

tasks.name: Review and refactor the CI jobs from what the Rust port taught us
tasks.description:
Go through `.github/workflows/` with the user and propose changes, based on what CI did during *The Rust port* and the first releases. Each change is agreed first: editing CI is the user's call.

## What to look at
- **What runs when:** pushes to a release branch run nothing unless dispatched (`gh workflow run CI --ref <branch>`); a PR runs again after every push. Is that still the right trade?
- **Time and caching:** a run takes about 4–5 minutes. Look at the cargo and pnpm caches, the jobs that build the dashboard and atm more than once (Rust ×3, `atm for the e2e suite`, Playwright), and whether artifacts could be shared instead.
- **The app (T-455 onwards)** is part of `cargo build`/`test`, so the Linux job needs the webview's system packages and Windows builds against WebView2. See what that adds to each job, and whether the e2e binary and the release should build only `-p atm-cli`.
- **Windows:** the suite runs only partly there (T-480, T-482), and the stress test fails (T-481). Decide what the Windows job checks until those are done.
- **macOS:** the stress test hit lock timeouts twice (T-481). Is that a slow runner or a real bug?
- **Screenshots:** CI makes missing Linux baselines, and the local scripts get a Linux atm (T-485). Check that the two use the same binary and the same steps.
- **Runner images:** `ubuntu-latest` moves to Ubuntu 26 (CI's annotation); the e2e binary is built on 22.04 for an older glibc. Pin the images we depend on.
- **Required checks:** the ruleset names jobs by their display names (`Rust (ubuntu-latest)`, …), so renaming a job breaks merges. Keep the names in one place, or test that `.github/rulesets/main.json` matches `ci.yml` (`ci-workflow.test.ts`).
- **Release workflows:** `release.yml`, `homebrew.yml` and `skills.yml` worked first time for 0.32.0 and 0.33.0. Note anything worth keeping in `packaging/README.md`.

## Outcome
The agreed changes in the workflows, `ci-workflow.test.ts` and `AGENTS.md`'s CI section, with `docs/security-architecture.md` updated if a permission or secret changes.

tasks.name: Overhaul atm's human-readable output: alignment, grouping and styling
tasks.description:
atm's plain output (without `--json`) is hard to scan. For example, `atm project status` prints the per-sprint, per-type and per-label counts as one long comma-separated line each, and the blocked and waiting lists as long lines joined with `;`. Make it read well in a terminal without changing what it says or what `--json` returns.

## First, a design with the user
Propose the look before changing code: a before/after of `atm project status`, `atm task list`, `atm task details`, `atm sprint list`, `atm release list` and `atm doctor`. Decide:
- **Alignment:** columns padded to the widest value (IDs, statuses, priorities), long names cut or wrapped to the terminal's width, and sections with a heading and indented lines instead of `a, b, c` runs.
- **Styling:** bold headings, colour for status kinds and priorities, dimmed secondary text. Only when standard output is a terminal; never with `NO_COLOR`, `--json`, or output going to a pipe or file.
- **What `project status` leads with:** the active sprint and what's next first; the long breakdowns (all sprints, types, labels) shorter, or behind a flag.
- **Dependencies:** terminal width and colour either hand-written or from a crate (e.g. `anstyle`, already in the tree through clap). Any new crate is proposed first.

## Agents read this output too
The skills relay what atm prints, and agents act on it. Keep it plain text when it isn't a terminal, keep each fact on a line agents can find, and check `docs/agent/` and the skills that quote output. A change to output agents act on follows AGENTS.md's security checklist (the written review in `docs/security-architecture.md` §3.3).

## Tests
The scenarios' exact `stdout` expectations change with the new layout: update them in one place per command. Add a test that a pipe gets no escape codes and that `NO_COLOR` turns colour off.

tasks.name: ADR-003: workspaces, the set of projects atm works on
tasks.description:
A design proposal, as an ADR, for a **workspace**: a set of projects atm works on, of which there may be several (usually one; others for tests, or work and personal projects).

## Why
The logic that works across projects (the project list with summaries, worktrees and logos; search across projects; skipping a broken project) lives in atm-api's HTTP routes, and the app (T-456) needs the same. atm-lib knows only one project; the registry is concrete in atm-db; boot is a bag of openers and JSON-in-git helpers ([layered-architecture.md](docs/layered-architecture.md) §3.2, §5.1, §11.2).

## The ADR
- Research: how atm's layers handle one project and many today; what the registry, `ATM_HOME`, `atm service`, the dashboard's routes and the app assume; how other tools model workspaces.
- Propose the workspace: what it is and holds, how one is chosen (default, `ATM_HOME`, a flag), the API's place for it (`api/v<N>/workspace/…`), the layers that own it, and how boot gets simpler.
- Diagrams in Mermaid. Options with trade-offs, a recommendation, consequences and a migration plan.

Reviewed with Hakan; T-456 waits for it.

notes.text: ADR-003 drafted (docs/adr/ADR-003-workspaces.md): workspaces as named lists over the home’s project index, chosen per call (flag > env > stored default), atm-lib’s Workspace with a ProjectOpener, boot as the composition root, api/v2/workspaces/<w>/…, a migration plan. Four questions for the review at the end.
Approved: Approved in Crit after one round (the task folder is the store’s, not the model’s)

ADR-003 accepted: workspaces in the state folder (platform app data, ATM_STATE_DIR), no project index, no boot (settings file + factories in atm-db and atm-vcs), atm workspace commands, api/v2/workspaces, a six-step migration.

tasks.name: Workspaces 4: the atm workspace commands

tasks.name: Rename a sprint: atm sprint rename

tasks.name: An older atm beside the new state folder: no projects lost, no server mistaken for ours
tasks.description:
T-490 moves `~/.agentic-task-manager` into the state folder once (`atm_common::home::move_legacy_state`), leaving a note. An atm from before (Homebrew 0.33.0, on the same machine as the app or a newer atm) still uses the old folder: it makes it again, with only the projects it registers from then on, and its dashboard shows just those (seen on Hakan's machine: the 0.33.0 server listed one project, the app all three). And the moved folder brought the old server's record along, so the new atm reports a server that serves the old folder as its own (`atm service status`).

## Change

- **The server record:** a record whose server serves another home (its whoami `home` isn't this state folder's) is not ours: `atm service` treats it as a stray of another atm, says so, and starts its own.
- **The link `atm service` prints** for a project is the page address (`/projects/<id>`), not the old `/#project=<id>`.
- Say in the 0.34.0 changelog and `packaging/README.md` that an older atm keeps the old folder, and how to tell (`atm version`).

## Tests
- atm-common: the legacy folder moved, then made again with a project: that project joins `default`.
- The CLI suite (`tests/scripts/serve.test.mjs` or `registry.test.mjs`): a record naming a server of another home isn't reported as this atm's.

tasks.name: Markdown and the layout in the app: Tauri's style nonce and connect-src (diagrams: T-503)
tasks.description:
In the app, a ```mermaid block never draws. Tauri puts the window's CSP on every HTML file it serves, CompMD's frame documents (`assets/compmd/<v>/compmd/strict.html`) included, and that policy had `frame-ancestors 'none'` (copied from `atm serve`'s page policy), so the frame was refused in the page. ## Change
- `frame-ancestors` out of the app's CSP (`app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`): the app's one window is its own, so it protects nothing there. Config only, no code.
- A test on what Tauri serves (its asset resolver): CompMD's frame document comes without `frame-ancestors`; the strict-CSP test updated.
- `docs/security-architecture.md` (I26) says why.

## Check
By hand in the real window (`cargo tauri dev`): the diagrams below draw, in this task's details and in Help. If the frame's scripts are still refused (it has an opaque origin; Tauri answers with the app's origin), decide the next step with Hakan.

**Found 2026-11-08 (Hakan, `cargo tauri dev`):** with `frame-ancestors` gone, Help still shows nothing where a diagram is, not even its code: the frame loads but its scripts don't run.

## Test diagrams

A flowchart:

```mermaid {alt="Draft, then review, then done"}
flowchart LR
  a[Draft] --> b[Review]
  b --> c{Approved?}
  c -- yes --> d[Done]
  c -- no --> a
```

A sequence diagram:

```mermaid {alt="The page asks the app, the app asks atm-lib"}
sequenceDiagram

  Page->>App: project_tasks
  App->>Lib: Member::tasks

```

A state diagram:

```mermaid {alt="A task's states"}
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> todo

  in_review --> done

```

One Mermaid can't read: it should show its code (the fallback), never nothing:

```mermaid

```

If it stays code or blank, the frame scripts are refused (opaque origin vs Tauri ACAO): decide the next step together.

tasks.name: Mermaid diagrams in the app: CompMD from a scheme of its own (tauri-plugin-compmd)
tasks.description:
Build the proposal of [CompMD in a Tauri app](docs/tauri-compmd-design.md#4-proposal-compmds-own-protocol-from-a-tauri-plugin), once Hakan has reviewed the document: a Tauri plugin serves CompMD's built folder on a `compmd:` scheme with the headers CompMD needs from a host (§3, H1–H5). ## Steps (§4.7)

tasks.name: CompMD's files from compmd:// after an upgrade: WebKit's custom-scheme cache
tasks.description:
A gap in [ADR-004](docs/adr/ADR-004-compmd-in-tauri-through-its-own-protocol.md): WebKit (WKWebView, on macOS and iOS) caches a custom URI scheme's responses, so a file replaced at the same path can keep running its old version (seen in another Tauri app's custom-scheme frames). ADR-004 keeps the paths CompMD's files have under `atm serve` (`/assets/compmd/<version>/…`). The CompMD version in the path changes with CompMD, but not when atm rebuilds the same CompMD version differently (its packs, `compmd.config.json`, a pack's built module), so after an atm upgrade the app could run the previous files from `compmd://`, and the page and its frames could speak different versions of the frame protocol.

## 1. Check it first
In the running app on macOS (`cargo run -p atm-app`, and a bundle): open a task with a diagram; replace a CompMD file the plugin serves (a frame's `runtime.js`, or the Mermaid pack's module) with a changed copy at the same path, one that shows it changed (a console line); rebuild, run again, open the task: does the old file still run? Record what each build showed.

## 2. If it does, fix it in `tauri-plugin-compmd`, as the plugin's default
The plugin is meant to move into CompMD for any Tauri host (ADR-004 decision 5), so the fix is its default behaviour, not atm's configuration. One of:
- **Content-hashed paths:** the plugin serves the build's CompMD folder under a name made from a hash of its files, gives the page that `base` (H4), and answers with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`; a changed file is then a new path;
- **or, if the paths must stay as under `atm serve`:** `Cache-Control: no-cache` with a validator (an `ETag` and `If-None-Match`, as `atm serve` sends) that WebKit honours for custom schemes; check in the app that it does.
Prefer the first if WebKit's handling of validators on custom schemes is uncertain.

## 3. Record it
- ADR-004: the result in its Risks; a decision if the plugin changes (and the design doc's §4.2 if its headers change).
- The plugin's header tests stay in step with `atm serve`'s (H1, H2: CORS `*`, `nosniff`, `sandbox allow-scripts` on frame documents); if the cache headers differ between the two, say why in both.

notes.text: Scope after T-503 (ADR-005): the frames are CompMD’s plugin’s, at content-hashed paths, so the cache can’t serve an old frame. What is left to check is atm’s own atm: scheme (assets.rs: compmd.js, its WebAssembly, the packs’ modules, at /assets/compmd/<version>/, no-cache). A stale pack module fails its hash check visibly; check compmd.js across a rebuild of the same CompMD version, and if it sticks, name the folder by a hash.

tasks.description:
`dev/0.35.0` to `main`, tagged, built, signed and published. The process is in [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md); the last one was T-509.

## On `dev/0.35.0`
- **Version:** `0.35.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** the `[Unreleased]` entries become `## [0.35.0] - <date>`; check they say what shipped (T-503 diagrams in the app with CompMD 0.6.0, T-506, T-483, T-508; T-510's design).
- **WHATS-NEW.md:** a `## [0.35.0]` entry, 3–6 plain bullets of at most 180 characters each (`release-notes.test.ts`): diagrams in the app, the app updating itself (from the next release on), the app showing changes as they happen.
- **Screenshots:** regenerate the Linux baselines once (`pnpm run test:e2e:visual:update`, Docker), and look at the ones that changed.
- **Security checklist** (`docs/security-architecture.md` §3): skills or `docs/agent/` changed since `main` → a written review in §3.3 instead of the live sandbox run. New entry points this release (the updater, which downloads and installs code; the app's subscription commands; the `atm:` scheme) are in the doc: check they describe what shipped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm run verify` in `dashboard/`; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo deny check` from the root.

## The PR
- Open it with `/atm-push`: `dev/0.35.0` to `main`. The required checks must pass.
- The user merges it, or says to merge it. Then record the merge (`atm vcs pushed --pr <n> --at <mergedAt>`).

## The release (with the user's go-ahead)
- `packaging/release.sh 0.35.0 --push` on an up-to-date `main`; watch the Release run. **The updater's artifacts are made for the first time** (the signed `.app.tar.gz` and `latest.json`): if the job fails, fix it on a branch and tag again, never by hand.
- Check the draft (the CLI's archives, the DMG, the app archive and its signature, `latest.json`, `SHA256SUMS`), then publish it; T-521 checks the updater's side with the user.
- Watch the Homebrew and Skills workflows (formula, cask with `auto_updates true`, skills `atm-v0.35.0`).
- Check with the user, on a Mac: `brew upgrade` gives 0.35.0, the app opens, diagrams draw in it.

tasks.name: Check atm's app against CompMD's redesigned Tauri plugin and its guidance for Tauri apps
tasks.description:
CompMD is redesigning `tauri-plugin-compmd` and how Tauri apps should use CompMD. **Waits for that redesign task in CompMD** (its release and its documentation for Tauri apps).

Once it's out, check atm's app against it and bring it up to the standard:

## What to compare
- **The plugin and its version:** `tauri-plugin-compmd` (pinned with `=` to the `@compmd/*` packages' version, `app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`), and how the app registers it (`app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`).
- **What atm serves itself on `atm:`** (`app/src-tauri/src/assets.rs`, embedded by `app/src-tauri/build.rs`): `compmd.js`, its WebAssembly and the packs' modules. Does the plugin now serve these, or say how an app should?
- **The page's side** (`dashboard/src/lib/compmd.ts`: `sandboxOptions`, `fetchPackModules`, `moduleUrl`): the frames' `base`, the packs' modules handed over as code checked by their `integrity`. Is this still the recommended way, or does CompMD's API cover it now?
- **The window's CSP** (`tauri.conf.json`, I26 in `docs/security-architecture.md`): the `atm://localhost/assets/compmd/` and `compmd://localhost/frames/` folders, and their `http://….localhost` forms for Windows.
- **Caching:** T-508 found WebKit asks again for each `atm:` file (`no-cache`); check against what CompMD now recommends.

## Then
Where atm differs from the standard: change it (or record why not), keeping `atm serve` and the app serving the same files with the same headers (`tests/scripts/compmd-host-headers.json`). Update [ADR-005](docs/adr/ADR-005-compmds-tauri-plugin-and-atms-asset-scheme.md) (or a new ADR replacing it), I26, and the [Tauri guide](docs/guides/tauri.md). New dependencies or plugin versions need a yes first.

## Checks
The app's Rust tests (`the_pages_compmd_files_come_from_atms_scheme_as_atm_serve_sends_them`, `the_windows_csp_is_strict`, `assets.rs`'s), `compmd.test.ts`, the app e2e specs, and by hand: diagrams draw in the app (`cargo tauri dev`, and a release bundle).
